html:
Jamilya is a short novel by the Kyrgyz writer Chinghiz Aitmatov, published in 1958. It is told by a teenage boy in a Kyrgyz village during the Second World War. His brother is away at the front, and the brother's young wife, Jamilya, falls in love with Daniyar, a quiet, wounded soldier, as they haul grain together to the railway station. In the end she leaves her husband's family and the village with him.

The French poet Louis Aragon translated it into French and called it the most beautiful love story in the world. That praise made Aitmatov famous across the Soviet Union and abroad.

The book stood out in Soviet literature for putting a woman's feelings above the custom of the clan, at a time when Kyrgyz tradition still bound a wife to her husband's family. The boy narrator, moved by what he has seen, becomes a painter. Aitmatov went on to write The White Ship and The Day Lasts More Than a Hundred Years, and his village tales carry the oral world of the Manas epic into the modern novel.
